Rule Description: On average, each warp of this workload spends 27.6 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently used data to shared memory. Stall samples are reported on the consumer instruction waiting for the result, not necessarily on the producer. When this reason dominates, the kernel is memory-latency-bound, which is not necessarily memory-bandwidth-bound; prefer latency-hiding changes such as ILP, unrolling, or pipelining when bandwidth is not saturated. This stall type represents about 67.7% of the total average of 40.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.
